chain.label: Deep marine layer producing regional low overcast and reduced visibility along route
chain.trigger: an unusually thick marine layer was present across the region, such that clouds associated with it extended up to 2,400 to 2,500 ft msl; controllers reported "an overcast ceiling of 1,100 ft agl" and "visibility of 2.5 miles"

chain.label: Rising mountainous terrain near Calabasas that pooled fog, with locally lower ceilings and visibility than reported
chain.trigger: "the topography in the area tended to channel fog up from the coast... that would stack up against the hills"; "the area near the accident site would have had lower ceilings and visibilities than those reported at VNY and CMA"

chain.label: Island Express incomplete SMS implementation; no documented policy or safety assurance review of flight risk analysis forms
chain.trigger: "Island Express had an SMS that was neither required by the FAA nor part of the company's FAA-approved or -accepted programs"; "The company did not implement the entire program as outlined in its SMS Manual."

chain.label: No formal preflight weather briefing and no updated flight risk analysis form at departure, so no DO consultation and no alternate plan
chain.trigger: "There was no record that the pilot obtained a formal preflight weather briefing"; "the accident pilot did not complete a new form before departing from SNA"

caused_by.evidence: "the company provided no documented policy or procedure regarding expectations such as... what criteria would require completion of a new form"
"weather observations for VNY included visibility of 2.5 miles..., which was less than what had been forecasted in the TAFs available at the time the pilot completed the flight risk analysis form"

chain.label: Pilot's self-induced pressure to fulfill the client's travel needs and plan continuation bias
chain.trigger: "the pilot's likely self-induced pressure and the pilot's plan continuation bias, which adversely affected his decision-making"

chain.label: Pilot continued VFR flight west along US 101 into deteriorating weather instead of diverting, turning back, or landing
chain.trigger: "the probable cause of this accident was the pilot's decision to continue flight under visual flight rules into instrument meteorological conditions"

caused_by.evidence: "cloud bases were between 1,300 and 1,400 ft msl and possibly lower in some areas near the accident site"
"Devising an alternative plan before departure would have aided the accident pilot's decision-making in flight concerning whether to continue the flight as originally planned or divert and land"

"the pilot's decision to continue the flight into deteriorating weather conditions was likely influenced by his self-induced pressure..., his lack of an alternative plan, and his plan continuation bias"

chain.label: Maintained about 140 kts at 400-600 ft agl in 1-1.5 mile visibility rather than slowing to maneuver
chain.trigger: "the pilot's poor decision to fly at an excessive airspeed for the weather conditions was inconsistent with his adverse-weather-avoidance training and reduced the time available for him to choose an alternative course of action"

caused_by.evidence: "The helicopter's flight path did not diverge from overflying US 101 until after the pilot had penetrated clouds"

chain.label: Helicopter penetrated cloud bases over US 101 and entered IMC; pilot lost outside visual reference
chain.trigger: "at the time that the pilot took action to initiate a climb, the helicopter had already begun penetrating clouds, and the pilot lost visual reference to the horizon and the ground"

caused_by.evidence: "there was no evidence that any dynamic or rapidly deteriorating weather phenomena were present that would have prevented the pilot from discontinuing the flight or changing his planned route"
"slowing the helicopter can reduce the closure rate between the helicopter and the adverse weather conditions... there was no evidence that he attempted to do so"
"a pilot flying VFR west above US 101 would likely enter dense fog rather suddenly near Mureau Road and then very quickly lose visual contact with US 101"

chain.label: Non-standard IIMC response: 1,500-fpm climbing left turn at high airspeed, no emergency declared, communication prioritized over aviating
chain.trigger: "The excessive airspeed and rapid climb rate the pilot used were inconsistent with his training for recovering from an entry into IMC. Also, the pilot did not declare an emergency"

caused_by.evidence: "the pilot announced to an ATC facility that he was initiating a climb to get the helicopter 'above the [cloud] layers,' and the helicopter immediately began climbing at a rate of about 1,500 fpm"

chain.label: Instrument scan interrupted by ATC radio exchange, IDENT button press, and looking outside for the cloud tops
chain.trigger: "The pilot's tasks associated with communicating with the controller and pushing the IDENT button introduced distractions from his primary task of monitoring the flight instruments while the helicopter was climbing in IMC"

caused_by.evidence: "the pilot's initiation of communication with the controller introduced a task load that continued for the remainder of the flight"

chain.label: Vestibular illusions (the leans in the steady left turn, somatogravic illusion during the accelerating descent) produced a false sense of attitude
chain.trigger: "the pilot experienced spatial disorientation while climbing the helicopter in instrument meteorological conditions"; "about 2 seconds into the helicopter's rapid descent, he advised the controller that it was climbing"

caused_by.evidence: "following the loss of visual cues in flight, pilots are susceptible to experiencing vestibular illusions, which can lead to spatial disorientation and a loss of control of the aircraft"
"Such interruptions in the pilot's instrument scan, as well as the introduction of head movements, would make him more vulnerable to misleading vestibular cues"
"the helicopter entered a steady left turn that was conducive for the pilot to experience a vestibular somatogyral illusion called the 'leans'"

chain.label: Loss of helicopter control: steepening left bank and rapid descent from 2,370 ft msl with no recovery
chain.trigger: "which led to his loss of helicopter control and the resulting collision with terrain"; "it began to descend rapidly while remaining in the left turn"

caused_by.evidence: "the pilot either was not referencing the helicopter's instruments or was having difficulty interpreting or believing them due to the compelling vestibular illusions, and he did not successfully recover the helicopter"

chain.label: Helicopter struck hilly terrain at about 1,100 ft msl and was destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: "entered a rapidly descending left turn and crashed into terrain in Calabasas, California"

caused_by.evidence: "he suddenly saw the descending helicopter emerge from the clouds and roll to the left... before it struck the terrain and erupted into flames"

chain.label: Pilot and eight passengers fatally injured
chain.trigger: "The pilot and the eight passengers died"; "The pilot's cause of death was blunt force trauma."
